
=================================================================
#6 Gunchogo, the 13th  (371)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: Part I — The Three Kingdoms / The King for All · place: pyongyang · tone: fairy-tale legend
Logline: A Baekje king marches north, and a Goguryeo king dies on his own wall. In seven hundred years, it never happens again.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Baekje’s thirteenth king marches north to Pyongyang. A Goguryeo king dies on his own wall. In seven hundred years, it never happens again.
[1] [CARD King Geunchogo: The king every later Baekje king quotes when he wants to sound brave.]
[2] [PLACE pyongyang: The north’s capital, and a long walk for anyone who wants it.]
[3] [MAP 371: Baekje at its height.]
[4] ¶ Baekje has the river, the coast and the sea roads east. The clans take the docks. The throne takes a cut. It is the richest kingdom in Samhan, and the strongest. Neither lasts.
[5] ¶ What its king wants is the one thing Baekje doesn’t have: the north’s capital. One winter he takes thirty thousand men up the frozen roads to get it.
[6] ── SCENE: The Camp ──
[7] ¶ The night before, the Baekje king sits by a fire below the wall with his son, the crown prince, who has never seen a city this big and is trying not to show it.
[8] The Crown Prince: They have a wall, Father. A real one. And a king on it.
[9] King Geunchogo: Good. I’d hate to walk this far for an empty one. / Nobody from the south has ever stood on that wall. Our grandsons will want to know who was first.
[10] The Crown Prince: And if he won’t come down?
[11] King Geunchogo: Then he’s braver than I am, and we’ll find out what that’s worth.
[12] ── SCENE: The Wall ──
[13] ¶ On the wall of Pyongyang there is a Goguryeo boy with a bow and not enough arrows. Beside him, in the same frozen mud, is his king.
[14] A Goguryeo Archer: Majesty, get down— they’ve found the range—
[15] The Goguryeo King: So have we. / A king who climbs off his wall teaches the whole wall to climb off. Shoot.
[16] ¶ The arrow that finds him isn’t aimed at anyone. It comes over the parapet the way rain does. He sits down in the mud as if he had decided to.
[17] The Goguryeo King: …Don’t tell them. / Not until they’ve gone home. Keep shooting.
[18] ¶ The boy tells no one. The gate stays shut. Below it, the Baekje king hears the wailing start inside the walls, and knows exactly what that sound is.
[19] King Geunchogo: That’s a king’s funeral. / …Turn them around. We came for a city. We’re going home with something better.
[20] ¶ On the road south the crown prince asks why they didn’t take the city. His father points back down the column. The men are already singing about it.
[21] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 18, Goguryeo Annals — King Gogugwon, yr. 41 (371)): Winter, tenth month. The king of Baekje came with thirty thousand men and attacked Pyongyang. The king led his troops out to meet them and was struck by a stray arrow. He died on the twenty-third day of that month.❞
[22] ¶ Back in the south they give him a chant, and the chant outlives everything else he won.
[23] Baekje: Restore the reign of the thirteenth Eraha.
[24] ¶ They will still be chanting that sentence three centuries later, in a courtyard, to a clever king who has already decided that a country is a story. It is the sentence that gets Daeya burned.
[25] ¶ Goguryeo remembers it too, and differently, and for exactly as long. The boy from the wall lives to be old. He tells it to his grandsons, and they tell theirs.
[26] ¶ **North, then, three hundred years on, to the snow and Goguryeo’s most frightening commander. First question: do you know what happens to traitors…?**
